newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Club agrees debt rescheduling for Madagascar.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club agrees debt rescheduling for Madagascar.

text.p: The Paris Club of creditor nations said on Wednesday it had agreed debt relief for Madagascar, offering it the most generous terms currently available to poor nations.
It said it had agreed relief amounting to a reduction of up to 67 percent of payments due on debt covered by the accord, under so called "Naples terms" available to poor, heavily indebted nations.
Creditor countries also agreed to meet in three years to consider a reduction of Madagascar's stock of debt, it said in a statement.
The debt relief covers debt payments falling due during a three-year economic reform programme agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) which runs to November, 1999.

The Paris Club, an informal grouping of official creditors and chaired by France, is also looking at improving debt relief available for poor nations in an initiative being carried out with the IMF and World Bank.
It has yet, however, to offer any country the improved terms, which were agreed in principle last year. The improved terms would offer a reduction on up to 80 percent of debt payments due.
